observed: The stub contract supports TIMEOUT, CANCELLATION_OR_CLIENT_DISCONNECT, MALFORMED_RESPONSE, HTTP_503, and TRANSPORT_FAILURE.
The 18-case preregistration schedules only one timeout/malformed fault matrix, and that matrix is explicitly the hook/bridge fault case.
No measured case or repetition maps the model-stub timeout, malformed response, HTTP 503, transport failure, or active cancellation controls.
The non-secret OpenHands configuration does not bind numRetries, retry waits, model timeout, or a per-case fault activation schedule.
The bound OpenHands LLM source defaults num_retries to 5 and timeout to 300 seconds.
findings.inferred: The current preregistration can offline-prove that fault controls exist but cannot prospectively prove which measured repetition activates them, how many model requests are permitted, or that cancellation and shutdown complete within a frozen deadline.
findings.impact: The design requirement that the deterministic stub support and measure timeout, cancellation, malformed, and transport failures is not reproducibly scheduled. Default retries could also violate one-request evidence and wall-clock bounds.
requiredRemediation: add prospectively frozen model-stub fault and cancellation cases or an equally explicit repetition schedule
bind exact model timeout and retry waits
bind the case-to-mode activation channel and expected request count
define cancellation trigger, future-completion deadline, client-disconnect evidence, process inventory, and cleanup oracle
repeat offline qualification against the successor configuration and harness

observed: The hook JUnit suite contains eight testcase elements and zero failure/error elements.

findings.impact: This does not negate the eight emitted passing testcase records, but the raw discrepancy must be disclosed rather than reported as an unqualified aggregate count.
requiredRemediation: report testcase-element and aggregate counts separately
do not claim 15 independently emitted hook test records
